He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]] before being selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 11th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. After spending his first seven seasons with the Trail Blazers, he was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in the 2019 off-season. He reached the [[NBA Finals]] with the Heat in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]]. No NBA player who is at least {{height|ft=7}} has a career [[three point shot]] [[field goal percentage]] of 40%, but Leonard is one of the few that has one over 39%. ==Early life== Leonard, born in [[Woodbridge, Virginia]],{{cite web | last = Klee| first = Paul| title = Meyers Leonard: A road less traveled | work = [[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)|The News-Gazette]] | date = June 1, 2010 | url = http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/mens-basketball/2010-06-01/meyers-leonard-road-less-traveled.html | access-date = September 23, 2016}} grew up in [[Robinson, Illinois]], a small town in southeastern Illinois. When he was six years old, his father James, a golf pro, was killed in a freak bicycle accident. His mother Tracie, once an athlete who would run upwards of 10 miles a day, had been largely housebound since her husband's death, due to an old horseback injury and subsequent disc surgery that left her with crippling pain.{{cite web |last=O'Neil |first=Dana |date=January 25, 2012 |title=Meyers Leonard shoulders plenty |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7501291 |access-date=January 11, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}} When he was in second grade, the young Leonard gained a surrogate family. Brian Siler, an insurance agent in Robinson who had a son of the same age, was aware of Leonard's family situation, and eventually became a father figure. Leonard regularly attended the Silers' church and went on family vacations. According to ''[[ESPN.com]]'' writer Dana O'Neil:
"Looking to shoehorn the relationship into a convenient box, outsiders have called this Meyers' version of ''The Blind Side'', but the comparison is inaccurate. [[The Blind Side: Evolution of a Game|The book]] and [[The Blind Side (film)|subsequent movie]] tell the story of [[Michael Oher]], a boy who was homeless and didn't have much of a family life. Meyers Leonard has a family. It has not abandoned him. On the contrary, Tracie loves her son, loves him so much that she was willing to accept help."
==High school career== Leonard entered high school as a [[guard (basketball)|guard]], but was converted to center after a {{convert|6|in|cm|adj=on|spell=in}} growth spurt between his freshman and sophomore years. O'Neil called him "something of a basketball anomaly", adding that Leonard "gained all that height without losing his coordination or his fast-twitch muscles." In high school, Leonard was named a member of the 2010 Illinois All-State Team as selected by the [[Associated Press]], ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'', ''[[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)|News-Gazette]]'', and the Illinois Basketball Coaches Association. Leonard led Robinson High School to the [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] class 2A state championship{{cite web|title=Class 2A championship: Derek Hannahs cashes in on overtime opportunities The pair spent two hours of shooting basketball and then three hours of talking, since she refused a dinner date.{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/timcasey/2020/10/05/how-miami-heat-center-meyers-leonard-and-his-wife-elle-leonard-built-a-health-food-company/?sh=6676148e4c48|title=How Miami Heat Center Meyers Leonard And His Wife, Elle, Built A Health Food Company|accessdate=March 25, 2023|date=October 5, 2020|work=[[Forbes]]|last=Casey |first=Tim}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2012–2019)=== Leonard was drafted with the 11th overall pick by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. On July 13 he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Trail Blazers.{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2012 |title=Damian Lillard, Meyers Leonard sign Trail Blazers rookie contracts |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2012/07/damian_lillard_meyers_leonard_sign_trail_blazers_r.html |website=oregonlive}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2012/7/13/3157265/blazers-officially-announce-signings-of-damian-lillard-meyers-leonard|title=Blazers Officially Announce Signings Of Damian Lillard & Meyers Leonard|first=Ben|last=Golliver|date=July 13, 2012|website=Blazer's Edge}} On October 31, 2012, Leonard made his NBA debut, logging 23 minutes and scoring four points against the [[2012–13 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400277732|title=Lakers vs. Trail Blazers - Game Recap - October 31, 2012 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} He made his first career start on November 21, 2012, against the [[2012–13 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]], finishing with 12 points and 5 rebounds.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400277888|title=Trail Blazers vs. Suns - Game Recap - November 21, 2012 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} On March 30, 2013, he had a season-best game with 22 points and 10 rebounds in a loss to the [[2012–13 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leoname01/gamelog/2013/|title=Meyers Leonard 2012-13 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} [[File:Meyers Leonard Blazers 2013.jpg|thumb|Leonard with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in 2013]] Leonard's numbers dipped from his rookie to sophomore season, falling behind fellow second-year big man [[Joel Freeland]] as the primary backup to starter [[Robin Lopez]]. He saw action in 29 fewer games in [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14]], with his minutes and points per game cut in half, as the Blazers transformed from a lottery team to a playoff contender.{{Cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2014/05/you_be_the_gm_trail_blazers_center_meyers_leonard.html|title=You be the GM: Trail Blazers center Meyers Leonard|first=Sean Meagher | The|last=Oregonian/OregonLive|date=May 22, 2014|website=oregonlive}} On January 2, 2014, he had a season-best game with 8 points and 10 rebounds in a 134–104 win over the [[2013–14 Charlotte Bobcats season|Charlotte Bobcats]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leoname01/gamelog/2014/|title=Meyers Leonard 2013-14 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} In [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15]], Leonard played only 13 total minutes in Portland's first 9 games as he was stuck in the big-man rotation behind Lopez, Freeland and [[Chris Kaman]]. On November 15, 2014, with [[LaMarcus Aldridge]] scratched with an upper respiratory illness against the [[2014–15 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]], Leonard picked up the start at power forward, playing 29 minutes. With his first major minutes at the power forward spot, he performed admirably, tallying 12 rebounds and hitting a three-pointer. He went on to pick up DNPs in 11 of the next 12 games. But when Lopez broke his hand going up for a rebound against the [[2014–15 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]] on December 15, Leonard got another chance to show that he deserved time on the court. His improvement was incremental, but noticeable, over the following seven weeks. His play while Lopez was out earned him time to prove himself. He only saw six DNPs after the turn of the year, and grew in confidence despite limited minutes. At the season's end, Leonard had produced a remarkable 50/40/90 season, shooting 51% from the field, 42% from three-point range, and 93% from the free throw line.{{Cite web |last=Sampson |first=Peter |date=May 22, 2015 |title=Meyers Leonard: From Afterthought to Folk Hero |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2015/5/22/8641991/meyers-leonard-season-review-portland-trail-blazers |access-date=January 11, 2024 |website=Blazer's Edge}} In the penultimate game of the regular season on April 13, he scored a career-high 24 points in a loss to the [[2014–15 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |date=April 14, 2015 |title=Westbrook scores 36; Thunder beat Trail Blazers 101-90 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400579501 |access-date=January 11, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}} He went on to record a playoff-best game with 13 points and 13 rebounds in a win over the [[2014–15 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]] in game 4 of Portland's first-round series. The Blazers lost the series 4–1.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leoname01/gamelog/2015/|title=Meyers Leonard 2014-15 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} On or taller. While [[Dirk Nowitzki]] has the highest number of made three point shots by a player listed at {{height|ft=7}} or taller with 1,982 made, Nowitski's career percentage is only 38%. Meanwhile, Leonard had a career percentage over 39%,{{cite web|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/barry-jackson/article240244831.html|title=Sports Buzz Heat’s Duncan Robinson on verge of NBA history. ==Personal life== Leonard has two older brothers; Christian Juracich, who died in 2020 and Bailey Leonard, a former [[U.S. Marine]] who has served in [[Afghanistan]].{{Cite web |title=Marine surprises brother after not seeing him for 2 years |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DsUo5ZToBM4 |via=YouTube.com}} On May 25, 2014, he proposed marriage to [[Elle Leonard|Elle]], his long-time girlfriend, who accepted. They were married at the beginning of August 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nba/see-which-portland-trail-blazers-showed-up-at-meyers-leonards-wedding|title=See which Portland Trail Blazers showed up at Meyers Leonard's wedding|accessdate=April 9, 2023|date=August 5, 2015|work=[[Fox Sports]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2015/08/trail_blazers_meyers_leonard_is_off_the_market_a_l.html|title=Trail Blazers' Meyers Leonard is off the market: A look at his wedding|accessdate=April 9, 2023|date=August 4, 2015|work=[[The Oregonian]]|last=Freeman |first=Joe}} The Leonards founded a sports bar company together called Level Foods.{{Cite web|url=https://levelfoods.com/pages/about|title=OUR STORY|website=LEVEL|access-date=March 6, 2020|archive-date=August 7, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807155352/https://levelfoods.com/pages/about|url-status=dead}} On June 7, 2022, their son Liam Walter Leonard was born.{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CekET1pJG_N/|title=@meyersleonard post|accessdate=March 29, 2023|date=June 8, 2022|publisher=[[Twitter]]|last=Leonard |first=Meyers}} Their second son, Jackson James Leonard was born May 14, 2025. In April 2019, Leonard invested in [[FaZe Clan]] as a content creator.{{Cite web|url=https://esportsobserver.com/meyers-leonard-faze-clan/|title=NBA Player Meyers Leonard Announces Investment In FaZe Clan|last=Duran|first=H. B.|date=April 11, 2019|website=The Esports Observer|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412064819/https://esportsobserver.com/meyers-leonard-faze-clan/|archive-date=April 12, 2019|access-date=January 21, 2020}} The Leonards have donated $500,000 to the Illinois Athletic Department toward the renovation of the site of their first date, the Ubben Basketball Complex.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2621221880|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2472205047}}|title=Leonard: 'I was a fool' Former Illini 'taking steps to educate myself'|work=[[The Pantagraph]]|last=Anderson |first=Kimball|accessdate=March 30, 2023|date=January 20, 2022}} ===Antisemitic slur controversy=== On March 9, 2021, Leonard received criticism for using the [[Antisemitism|antisemitic]] slur "[[kike]]" during a [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]] stream while playing ''[[Call of Duty: Warzone (2020 video game)|Call of Duty: Warzone]]''. The Heat announced the same day that they were reviewing the matter and that Leonard would be "away from the team indefinitely."{{Cite news|last=Joseph|first=Andrew|date=March 9, 2021|title=The Heat's Meyers Leonard said an anti-Semitic slur during a Twitch stream|work=[[USA Today]]|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2021/03/heat-meyers-leonard-said-anti-semitic-slur-twitch-stream|access-date=March 9, 2021}} The [[eSports]] organization [[FaZe Clan]] cut ties with him later that day,{{cite web |last=Cooke |first=Hunter |title=FaZe Clan 'cutting ties' with NBA player Meyers Leonard over use of anti-Semitic slur during Warzone stream |url=https://dotesports.com/news/nba-player-meyers-leonard-uses-anti-semitic-slur-during-warzone-stream |website=Dot Esports |date=March 9, 2021}} although he remained an investor.{{Cite news|last=Smith|first=Noah|title=Meyers Leonard slur incident prompts a question: What's a FaZe 'member'?|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/video-games/esports/2021/03/15/faze-clan-meyers-leonard/|access-date=March 25, 2021|date=March 15, 2021}} He later apologized for using the slur, stating that he did not know what it meant.{{cite web |last=Kalland |first=Robby |title=Meyers Leonard Claimed He 'Didn't Know' What The Slur He Used Meant
